newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Feb industry sales down 2.35 pct vs Jan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Feb industry sales down 2.35 pct vs Jan.

text.p: Brazilian industry sales in February were down a seasonally adjusted 2.35 percent in February compared with January, the private National Confederation of Industry (CNI) said.
Excluding seasonal factors, February sales levels were 4.82 percent lower than in January, the CNI said in a statement.
"Although the contraction was expected given the characteristics of the period, the percentage drop is greater than what can be explained by purely seasonal factors," the statement said.
"The slowing down in industrial activity seems to reflect the end of a cycle of recovery in demand, which was based on growing consumer credit and prevailed through 1996," it added.
On a year-on-year basis industrial sales had risen, the CNI said.
February sales were 3.18 percent higher than in the same month last year.
Accumulated sales during the first two months of 1997 were 6.49 percent higher than in the same period last year.
The number of people employed in industry were down a seasonally adjusted 0.54 percent in February compared with January and were 3.86 percent lower than in the same month last year.
Industry was working at a seasonally adjusted 77.6 percent of capacity, down from 78.5 percent in January, the statement said.
The CNI represents Brazil's manufacturing industry.
